newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weaker at 26.375 to US dlr.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weaker at 26.375 to US dlr.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed weaker at 26.375 to the dollar on weekend arbitrage play, month-end book-closing and a mild speculative selling on continued spillover of Thailand's financial problems.
However, the Central Bank was firm in defending the peso at 26.375, selling more than $100 million out of the total $299 million traded for the day.
The peso closed at 26.374 to the dollar on Thursday.
One trader said the early morning weakness was caused by the usual arbitrage play as traders took advantage of swap points earned over the weekend.
Deals done on Friday are settled on Monday, providing dollar buyers to hold on to their pesos and earn a relatively higher interest rate.
Another trader said some banks have been nudging up the exchange rate to post higher revaluation done every end of the month for their foreign currency assets.
"It's the usual month-end window dressing," he said.
The dollar-buying trend snowballed in the afternoon after some foreign banks revived the ghost of Thai baht crisis by speculating that the peso would depreciate soon.
"The peso was under pressure again. It's the spillover effect again. Some foreign banks are still anticipating for the peso to fall," a trader from a foreign bank said.
Traders said they believed the peso would hit its support at 26.375 next week because to the strong defense of the Central Bank.
